set.n: Dr. Joseph Scheuermann's money jars, 541 Third St, Milwaukee (found 1902; possibly a hoax)
set.st: In Aug 1902 the woman then living at 541 Third St dug up bottle after bottle of coins and paper money in the back yard, said to have been buried there over about 15 years by the late Dr. Joseph Scheuermann; early reports put it at about $7,000, with charts in the bottles showing about $10,000 buried. His widow claimed the money. By the 1905 account she had found fully $3,000 sealed in medicine jars. In 1905 the same woman was charged with embezzlement and owed other creditors, which raised doubt that the 1902 bottles story was true. The widow threatened suit but never sued, and the finder soon traded the lot for a farm. Either the money was all dug up in 1902, or the find was a cover story for her borrowing; nothing is left to look for either way.
set.t: Found or faked in 1902; urban lot built over. History marker only.
set.tovw: Grade F (treasure thread): found in 1902, or a cover story; nothing left to look for
